name: Basilica of St. Mary of the Assumption (Lancaster, Ohio)
history: The first Mass in Lancaster was said by the Dominican Edward Fenwick, later the first bishop of Cincinnati, in a parishioner's home. The parish was founded around 1818-19 and its first frame church dedicated at Easter 1819. The cornerstone of the present church was laid in 1859; the Civil War slowed the work, which went on thanks to wealthy parishioners. It was consecrated on 5 June 1864 and became a basilica in 2022.
arch: A red-brick Gothic Revival church with a tall central tower and pinnacles.
features: It was the 91st U.S. basilica, the seventh in Ohio and the first in the Diocese of Columbus.
Dominican Sisters began teaching at the parish school in 1872.

look.d: The tower dominates the brick front.
Construction continued through the war thanks to generous parishioners.

fun: The pastor who began it, Father Lange, died months before it was completed.
journal: Built through the Civil War on the parish's own grit. Lancaster's brick Gothic.
